drafted_from: tool:give-a-buyer-a-paid-file-link's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Give a buyer a short-lived link to a file they paid for, and refuse anyone who has not paid", with {"object_key":"no-such-file.pdf","subject":"buyer@example.com"}. It runs tool:give-a-buyer-a-paid-file-link and answers {"status":"unavailable","reason":"governing-item-missing"}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (paid-file, payment-event, record:commercial-offer, access-grant, access-effect-rule, effect-lifecycle) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Give a buyer a short-lived link to a file they paid for, and refuse anyone who has not paid", and give it object_key (The file the buyer asks for, like "chapter-one.pdf"); subject (The account the door verified from the buyer's session, named the way your access rules name a buyer; empty for no session).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:give-a-buyer-a-paid-file-link and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads the file's paid-file record and answers grant with a link that expires (the record's ttl_seconds, else 3600), only when the subject is a verified account and holds any of the file's required access refs now (worked out as tool:see-who-holds-paid-access works it out).

4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: paid-file (records:read); payment-event (records:list); record:commercial-offer (records:list); access-grant (records:list); access-effect-rule (records:list); effect-lifecycle (records:list).
